14.0.0.en: God declared to Moses, the leader of the people, the rite for the cleansing of the leper. It begins with one of the acquaintances or family of the leper telling the priest that he has been healed, and bringing him to the priest outside the camp. The family of the leper signifies the Church, which brings sinners to Christ, the Great High Priest, to cleanse them from all their sins.

14.1.0.en: The priest goes out to the leper outside the camp, where his family has brought him to him. The going out of the priest signifies the Incarnation of Christ and His going out outside the camp to die for our sins; it is He who drew near to us to redeem and cleanse us.

14.1.1.en: The priest examines the leper, and if he finds that the leprosy has left his skin, he begins the rite of cleansing with him.

14.1.2.en: May we care for sinners and those who are far away, offering them love and encouraging them to be joined to the Church, and may we make the priests aware of their circumstances so that they may care for them. Just as the four carried their paralyzed friend, let us carry our brethren to Christ, so that they may find healing from all their troubles and may be established and rejoice in the Church.

14.2.0.en: Two birds ... clean: in some translations, two clean fowls; the meaning is two clean birds or two clean sparrows, because sparrows are among the clean birds.

14.2.1.en: Cedar wood: a piece of wood from the tall cedar trees that are abundant in Palestine and Lebanon. Scarlet: a piece of cloth of a dark red color.

14.2.2.en: Hyssop: a small, weak plant with small leaves, resembling the parsley plant.

14.2.3.en: The leper is cleansed on the first day by bringing two birds, which either the rich or the poor can bring because they are cheap. Birds signify loftiness because they fly toward heaven, like the loftiness of Christ the Redeemer and the loftiness that the leper should display in his new life.

14.2.4.en: They also bring a piece of cedar wood, which signifies the wood of the Cross, and also loftiness, because of the height of cedar trees.

14.2.5.en: Likewise a piece of scarlet cloth, which signifies the blood of Christ the Redeemer.

14.2.6.en: And also a bunch of the delicate little hyssop plant, which signifies the humility that appeared in Christ and that the leper should display in order to be cleansed.

14.3.0.en: Running water: flowing water like the water of rivers, not stagnant water like that of marshes. The bird is killed over it because the blood of a bird is little, so by mixing it with the water, the things that will be mentioned in (v. 6) can be dipped in it. The priest kills one of the birds outside the camp, far from the tabernacle of the congregation and the bronze altar, for the two birds offered are not among the known sacrifices offered on the bronze altar; rather, this is a special law for the cleansing of the leper.

14.3.1.en: The killing is done in an earthen vessel filled with running water, so that the blood of the bird, which is little, falls on this water.

14.3.2.en: The earthen vessel signifies the divine Incarnation, the water signifies the work of the Holy Spirit and the sacrament of Baptism, and the slain bird signifies Christ the Redeemer crucified on the Cross.

14.4.0.en: The priest takes the second bird, which is still alive, together with the piece of cedar wood, the scarlet and the hyssop plants. He may bind them together, or hold the three together in his hand, and dips them in the blood of the bird mixed with the running water, because the living bird signifies the risen Christ, yet bearing the marks of the wounds that were inflicted on the Cross, as the Book of Revelation mentions (Rev 5:6).

14.5.0.en: He sprinkles the water mixed with blood, in which the hyssop, the scarlet and the living bird were dipped, on the leper seven times. This signifies the fullness of the cleansing, because the number "7" signifies the week, that is, the fullness of life, so that the cleansed leper lives a new life with God all his days. It also signifies the Holy Spirit, who gives complete purity, as He cleanses us through the seven sacraments of the Church. Then the priest lets the living bird go, directing it toward the wilderness. This signifies the risen Christ, as we said, who rose to raise us up, we who live in the wilderness of the world, and to lift us up to the heavens.

14.6.0.en: After this the leper takes steps to complete his cleansing. This shows the importance of spiritual striving alongside the work of divine grace that is accomplished by Christ the Redeemer. These steps are:

14.6.1.en: 1- The leper washes his clothes, as a symbol of the purity of the conduct he will live after his healing from the disease.

14.6.2.en: 2- He shaves off all his hair, as a sign of ridding himself of all sins through repentance.

14.6.3.en: 3- He bathes in water, which signifies the two sacraments of Baptism and confession.

14.6.4.en: 4- The leper stays inside the camp, but not in his tent; rather, in a special place for seven days, as a symbol of the importance of the sojourn in the world in which the cleansed leper should live, that is, that he should not be absorbed in material desires lest he fall again into one of the sins. The number "7" signifies the fullness of life, that is, that he should live all his life without attachment to material things.

14.6.5.en: Repentance is not a word you say; rather, it is steps you must pass through: keeping away from the sources of sin, clinging to the Church, practicing the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, and then living in asceticism, using the world but without being absorbed in it.

14.7.0.en: Of the first year: one year old.

14.7.3.en: On the eighth day of the cleansing of the leper he offers sacrifices and offerings. The eighth day signifies eternity, that is, that he lives pure all his life, and then this extends forever in heaven.

14.7.4.en: It is noted that the leper now offers the sacrifices and offerings himself for the first time after his healing, because he has entered the camp. This signifies the importance of spiritual striving as long as a person is able to carry out the practices of spiritual striving, such as fasting and prostrations (metanoias) ...

14.7.5.en: The cleansed man brings four kinds of offerings, which are:

14.7.6.en: 1- A lamb for the trespass offering, which must be sound, that is, without blemish, because Christ our Redeemer is without blemish. He offers a trespass offering because he may have sinned against God and His laws or wronged others; these wrongs are also directed against God, in addition to his failure in worship and in offering the sacrifices at the feasts, because he was sick and isolated outside the camp.

14.7.7.en: 2- A ewe as a sin offering, for the sins he committed that caused him this disease. He offers a ewe, that is, a female, because the female gives birth and yields offspring, that is, fruits; this signifies the removal of sins and all their fruits and the beginning of the new life with its spiritual fruits.

14.7.8.en: 3- A second lamb for the burnt offering, so that God may be pleased with the sick man, from whom, because of his sin, the face of God was hidden, and may be pleased with him through this burnt offering, which signifies Christ, through whom we were reconciled with heaven.

14.7.10.en: a- Three tenths of fine flour; one tenth is offered with each of the trespass offering, the sin offering and the burnt offering. These signify the pure life of Christ that He lived on earth, and point to the new, pure life in which the healed sick man wants to live with God.

14.7.11.en: b- A log of oil, which is pure olive oil, used in the offerings presented to God because of its purity; it signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who will work in this healed sick man in his new life.

14.8.0.en: The priest in charge of the cleansing of the leper brings the healed sick man who stands before God to be cleansed, and places in his hands the slaughtered lamb to offer as a trespass offering, and the log of oil with one tenth of the flour mingled with oil, and waves them before God. That is, he moves his hands forward and backward, to the right and to the left, offering them to God who fills every place and is present in the four directions; and he lifts his hands up and then down, that is, he offers them to God who dwells in heaven, and lowers them down, that is, offered on his behalf.

14.9.0.en: The trespass offering is slaughtered, like the sin offering and the burnt offering, before the bronze altar at the entrance of the tabernacle of the congregation. The one who offers it does not eat of it; rather, he offers a part to God and the rest to the priest, that is, it is all holy to God and His priest. With it he offers one tenth of the flour, according to the rite of the grain offering mentioned in (ch. 2).

14.10.0.en: The Jewish scholars say that two priests performed this service. One of them gathers the blood in a basin and sprinkles it around the altar, according to the rite of the sacrifice mentioned in (ch. 5), while the other priest takes some of the blood and anoints the tip of the ear of the one offering the sacrifice, as a symbol of the sanctification of his hearing, that is, that he should take care to listen to pure conversations; then he anoints with the blood the thumb of his right hand, as a symbol of the sanctification of his works, because the right hand represents strength and the thumb is the most important finger. Then he anoints the great toe of his right foot, as a symbol of the sanctification of his conduct, that is, that he should walk in the way of God. Of course, one priest can perform this service, gathering the blood and then anointing the one offering the sacrifice.

14.11.0.en: The priest takes the log of oil, that is, the vessel in which the oil is, and pours it into his left hand. Then with the finger of his right hand he sprinkles some of this oil seven times toward the bronze altar and the sanctuary, that is, he presents the work of the Holy Spirit, who is signified by the number "7", before God to cleanse the sick man.

14.12.0.en: The priest takes some of the remaining oil in his left hand and anoints the right ear of the cleansed man, the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot, on top of the blood with which they were anointed before, as a symbol of the sanctification by the Holy Spirit of what he hears, what he does and the way he walks.

14.13.0.en: The priest pours the rest of the oil in his left hand on the head of the cleansed man, and this signifies the cleansing of his thoughts.

14.14.0.en: The priest offers the ewe, the sin offering for the cleansed man, and with it one tenth of the flour mingled with oil, by the same rite mentioned in (ch. 4); then he offers the lamb of the burnt offering, and with it one tenth of the flour mingled with oil, by the same rite mentioned in (ch. 1). Thus is completed the cleansing of the leper whom God healed.

14.14.1.en: So that you may live pure, take care to keep your eyes away from unclean sights, direct your hearing to pure words, and be careful in your works and conduct. And when God sees your care, He fills you with His love, and you feel Him in your life and rejoice with Him.

14.14.2.en: (b) The cleansing of the poor leper (vv. 21-32):

14.14.3.en: 21 "And if he be poor, and cannot get so much; then he shall take one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, to make an atonement for him, and one tenth deal of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering, and a log of oil; 22 And two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, such as he is able to get; and the one shall be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering. 23 And he shall bring them on the eighth day for his cleansing unto the priest, unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, before the LORD. 24 And the priest shall take the lamb of the trespass offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them for a wave offering before the LORD: 25 And he shall kill the lamb of the trespass offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot: 26 And the priest shall pour of the oil into the palm of his own left hand: 27 And the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before the LORD: 28 And the priest shall put of the oil that is in his hand upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the trespass offering: 29 And the rest of the oil that is in the priest's hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the LORD. 30 And he shall offer the one of the turtledoves, or of the young pigeons, such as he can get; 31 Even such as he is able to get, the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, with the meat offering: and the priest shall make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed before the LORD. 32 This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to get that which pertaineth to his cleansing." The place of the trespass offering (v. 28): the right ear, the thumb of the right hand and the great toe of the right foot, anointed with the blood.

14.14.4.en: God's mercy appears in not burdening the poor who were struck with leprosy and healed by God: they offer sacrifices and offerings of lesser cost, yet through them obtain complete cleansing. The difference between the offering of the poor man and that of the ordinary or rich person lies in two things:

14.14.5.en: 1- Instead of offering a ewe as a sin offering and a lamb for the burnt offering, the poor man offers a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

14.14.6.en: 2- Instead of offering three tenths of fine flour mingled with oil, the poor man offers only one tenth of fine flour mingled with oil.

14.14.7.en: The rest of the rite of the cleansing of the leper is carried out as already explained in this chapter, from (vv. 10-20).

14.14.8.en: May you feel for those around you, not only the poor but also everyone who suffers spiritual or psychological weakness. Do not burden anyone; honor everyone and encourage them, so that you may be tender like God and obtain His mercies.

14.14.9.en: (c) The cleansing of leprosy in houses (vv. 33-53):

14.14.10.en: 33 And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, 34 "When ye be come into the land of Canaan, which I give to you for a possession, and I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession; 35 And he that owneth the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, It seemeth to me there is as it were a plague in the house: 36 Then the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest go into it to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made unclean: and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house: 37 And he shall look on the plague, and, behold, if the plague be in the walls of the house with hollow strakes, greenish or reddish, which in sight are lower than the wall; 38 Then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days: 39 And the priest shall come again the seventh day, and shall look: and, behold, if the plague be spread in the walls of the house; 40 Then the priest shall command that they take away the stones in which the plague is, and they shall cast them into an unclean place without the city: 41 And he shall cause the house to be scraped within round about, and they shall pour out the dust that they scrape off without the city into an unclean place: 42 And they shall take other stones, and put them in the place of those stones; and he shall take other morter, and shall plaister the house. 43 And if the plague come again, and break out in the house, after that he hath taken away the stones, and after he hath scraped the house, and after it is plaistered; 44 Then the priest shall come and look, and, behold, if the plague be spread in the house, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean. 45 And he shall break down the house, the stones of it, and the timber thereof, and all the morter of the house; and he shall carry them forth out of the city into an unclean place. 46 Moreover he that goeth into the house all the while that it is shut up shall be unclean until the even. 47 And he that lieth in the house shall wash his clothes; and he that eateth in the house shall wash his clothes. 48 And if the priest shall come in, and look upon it, and, behold, the plague hath not spread in the house, after the house was plaistered: then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed. 49 And he shall take to cleanse the house two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop: 50 And he shall kill the one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water: 51 And he shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running water, and sprinkle the house seven times: 52 And he shall cleanse the house with the blood of the bird, and with the running water, and with the living bird, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet: 53 But he shall let go the living bird out of the city into the open fields, and make an atonement for the house: and it shall be clean."

14.15.0.en: Buildings too are liable to be struck with the disease of leprosy. But they now live in the wilderness of Sinai in tents, so God lays down for them a law about leprosy in the houses that they will build in the land of Canaan and live in, and about what they are to do if these are struck with leprosy.

14.16.0.en: If the owner of the house notices any strange appearance in the walls or ceiling of his house, he tells the priest what he saw.

14.17.0.en: The priest orders the house to be emptied of everything in it, because if he went to the house and judged that it was leprosy, everything in it would become unclean; but if they take these things out before the priest enters, they are counted clean and can be used.

14.18.0.en: The symptoms that give rise to suspicion of the disease of leprosy are defined by the Law in two appearances:

14.18.1.en: 1- A patch inclining to greenish or reddish.

14.18.2.en: 2- A depression in the wall or hollows in it.

14.19.0.en: If the priest notices the preceding symptoms, he suspects that it is leprosy, but in order to be sure of it he shuts up the house for seven days.

14.20.0.en: If after seven days the priest notices that the depressed patch has spread in the walls of the house, he suspects that it is leprosy, but it may be limited to a certain area, so he commands the following:

14.20.1.en: 1- Taking out the stones in this area where the patch is and casting them outside the city in an unclean place, that is, not the place where the holy ashes of the sacrifices are cast.

14.20.2.en: 2- Scraping the wall around these stones, gathering this dust and casting it also outside the city in an unclean place.

14.20.3.en: 3- They put new stones in place of the first ones, and put on them the dust mixed with water that holds the stones fast, like the mortar used today, and they also coat the stones with clay to fill the cracks. All this signifies rejecting sin by repentance and confession, and then beginning the new life with spiritual practices and good works.

14.21.0.en: If leprosy appears in the walls of the house after all of the above, that is, after pulling out the affected stones and putting in new dust, the priest judges that the house is struck with a fretting leprosy, that the partial treatment did not succeed with it, and he commands that the house be pulled down completely and all its stones and timber cast in an unclean place outside the city. This signifies keeping away from evil and everything connected with it.

14.22.0.en: If anyone enters, for any reason, a house suspected of being struck with leprosy which the priest has shut up for seven days, the one who entered against the priest's orders becomes unclean, even if he entered for only one minute, and remains unclean until the evening, and then he bathes and is clean.

14.23.0.en: But whoever is careless and enters the house during the period of suspicion that it is struck with leprosy, and sits and eats, that is, spends a period of time inside it, is unclean until the evening, and in order to be cleansed he must not only bathe but also wash his clothes. This signifies calling oneself to account through repentance for every carelessness.

14.24.0.en: If the suspicion of leprosy has been treated by putting in new stones and dust, and no symptoms of leprosy appear afterward, the priest judges the house to be clean.

14.25.0.en: After the affected stones and the dust around them have been changed and the priest has judged that the house is healed of leprosy, the rite of cleansing is performed for the house. It is the same rite performed for the leper on the first day, which was explained earlier in (vv. 1-7) of this chapter.

14.26.0.en: Here he states that what was mentioned in this chapter and the preceding chapter are the laws of the disease of leprosy in its various forms.

14.26.1.en: Take care that your house is pure, so that this may help you toward a life of purity. Let it be adorned with holy icons, let holy melodies be heard in it, and let everything done in it befit the presence of Christ in it. Then you will live pure, and everyone who enters your house will rejoice and receive a blessing.

14.26.28.en: The law of the issue: introduction:

14.26.29.en: In this chapter he speaks of the man from whose reproductive organs semen flows in a diseased manner for a number of days, and also of the natural emission in physical relations. He also speaks of the flow of blood from the reproductive organs of the woman in the normal state, that is, the monthly period, and also in the diseased state, which continues for longer periods. All of the above is considered uncleanness, and he provides the cleansing and treatment particular to each case. God cares about these matters and counts them as uncleanness in the Old Testament for the following reasons:

14.26.30.en: 1- With the Fall of man, sin spread in the human race and all became condemned to death, and the means of producing offspring is the reproductive organs; therefore what comes out of him is considered unclean, because it produces children born in sin.

14.26.31.en: 2- The issue signifies a lack of discipline in material desires, so God alerts us to be scrupulously careful so that He may protect us from falling into various desires.

14.26.32.en: 3- The aspect of health, that is, care for the cleanliness of these organs for the sake of propriety. This last meaning is what remains in the New Testament, after Christ lifted the sentence of death by His redemption, and the uncleanness was removed.
